title: Unlearning-Based Safeguards x Knowledge Recovery: Auditing the Durability Claims Regulators Accept

original_idea.body:
# Unlearning-Based Safeguards x Knowledge Recovery: Auditing the Durability Claims Regulators Accept

**Problem:** Labs cite unlearning as a mitigation; shallow unlearning is recoverable. Governance crediting an unlearning claim inherits a mitigation that doesn't hold.

**Direction:** On a small open model with a public unlearning benchmark (WMDP/TOFU), apply a published unlearning method, measure knowledge recovery via relearning/paraphrase probes, cross-reference policy language.

**Why it matters:** Tests whether a credited mitigation survives a cheap adversary. Single GPU, open benchmarks.

**Relevant context:** arXiv:2412.07097; arXiv:2406.07358; Safety Gap Toolkit (arXiv:2507.11544).

theory_of_impact.reasoning: Strong chain: if a credited mitigation fails, governance is over-trusting dangerous-knowledge removal; concrete catastrophic (bio/cyber) scenario.

accessible_complexity.reasoning: Inherited methodology with public benchmark and toolkit; novice+mentor can run relearning probes on a single GPU.

narrow_scope.reasoning: Focused first deliverable (durability gap on one method+benchmark) though some multi-step setup.

counterfactual_value.reasoning: Model-organism-flavored audit of a policy assumption; neglected, external scrutiny, open weights.

low_compute.reasoning: Applying unlearning + relearning steps on a small model; single mid GPU days.

novelty.reasoning: Unlearning durability is actively studied; the governance-claim-audit framing may be partly open.

novelty_assessment.reasoning: Shallow-unlearning recovery is documented; tying it to credited policy claims is a fresher angle.
